29 The diagram shows a stationary wave on a stretched spring at an instant in time.
P
Q
stretched
spring
Two particles on the spring, P and Q, are shown.
Which statement about the vibrations of P and Q is correct?
A
They have different frequencies.
B
They have the same amplitudes.
C
They have different periods.
D
They are always in phase.

hints: Look at where P and Q sit on the diagram: P is at the crest and Q is on the same upper loop, both above the dashed equilibrium line and on the same side of the crossing point.
Recall how a stationary wave differs from a progressive wave: frequency and period are common to the whole pattern, but amplitude depends on distance from a node.
Check whether P and Q are separated by a node: particles in the same loop between two adjacent nodes reach maximum displacement and zero displacement at the same instants.
walkthrough: Identify the pattern from the diagram: the dashed line is the equilibrium position, P is at maximum transverse displacement and Q is part-way down toward the node, both in the same upper loop.
State the stationary-wave rule: every particle except at the nodes performs SHM with the same frequency $f$ and the same period $T$, where $T = 1/f$.
Compare amplitudes: amplitude is zero at a node and maximum at an antinode, so P near the antinode vibrates with larger amplitude than Q closer to the node.
Compare phase: all particles between the same pair of adjacent nodes have displacements in the same direction at any instant and pass through zero together, giving a phase difference of $0$.
Apply this to P and Q: they are not separated by a node, so they move up and down together even though their amplitudes differ. This is option D.

A.explanation: All vibrating particles in one stationary wave oscillate with the same frequency, so P and Q do not differ in frequency.

B.explanation: Amplitude in a stationary wave varies with position, and P at the crest has larger amplitude than Q nearer the node.

C.explanation: Period $T = 1/f$ is the same for all particles in the stationary wave, so P and Q have the same period.

D.explanation: P and Q lie in the same loop between adjacent nodes, so they pass through equilibrium together and move in the same direction.
